file-catalog-with-saved-data-01.graded_text: Saved data is reached through the same read, write, exact-edit, and delete-file tools used for source files and assets, as file paths such as JSON files. The catalog has no separate tools for records, entries, collections, or the database.

votes.e: C/project/docs/mcp-tools.md line 24: "There are no record-level tools such as `update_record`. Saved data uses `read_file`, `edit_file`, `write_files`, and `search_files`". Line 98: "Each saved-data collection that `fernpage.json` declares appears as one JSON file at `.data/<collection>.json`." The tool table at lines 13-22 has no record, entry, collection, or database tools.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-02.graded_text: No tool has a required idempotency key, revision or version token, or confirmation argument. Protection against stale writes is enforced by the server, for example by rejecting a write that would overwrite changes made since the agent's read and asking for a fresh read.

votes.e: C/project/docs/mcp-tools.md line 87: "The server guards against overwriting their changes, and no call has to carry a revision token". Line 91: "the write is refused with `conflict`. The message says to read the file again." Line 31: "There are no confirmation arguments." The write_files schema requires only path plus content or sourceUrl (lines 330-331), and edit_file requires only oldText and newText (line 378). Neither has an idempotency key or a version argument.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-03.graded_text: The design explains how a visitor's write made after the agent read a saved-data file survives the agent's later write of that file: it is merged safely or the agent's write fails with a conflict. A plain last-writer-wins replacement does not pass.

votes.e: C/project/docs/mcp-tools.md line 127: "Entries the caller didn't change keep whatever other writers did to them since that read. That includes entries visitors added or deleted. A visitor's RSVP that arrived after the agent's read survives the agent's write." Line 128: "If the caller and someone else both changed the same entry since that read, the file is refused with `conflict`".

file-catalog-with-saved-data-04.graded_text: Deleting files takes an explicit nonempty list of exact paths, deleting a whole site is its own tool, and no omitted argument widens a deletion or makes an update create a new site.

votes.e: C/project/docs/mcp-tools.md line 407: "\"paths\": { \"type\": \"array\", \"minItems\": 1, ..." (required). Line 415 refuses "any path that names a directory or uses a wildcard". Line 28: "`create_site` and `delete_site` are their own tools. A file write never creates a site, and a file delete never removes one. ... No argument decides either." The lines that came closest to breaking the assertion are line 192, "Leaving out `workspaceId` only widens a read", and line 245, an optional `directory` on list_files. Both are reads.

file-catalog-with-saved-data-05.graded_text: Writing a saved-data file as a whole is checked entry by entry against the site's declared write rules and validation, with the agent holding only the rights of the person it acts for, so replacing the whole file cannot make a change that person could not make one entry at a time.

votes.e: C/project/docs/mcp-tools.md line 112: the server "handles each changed entry as one SDK-style operation". Line 119: "Each change passes the same rules, validation, and quota that a single SDK write would. The agent acts as the site owner". Line 121: "If any entry change is refused, nothing in that file changes." The owner is the person the agent acts for (line 160: "`owner` (members of the site's workspace)").

file-catalog-with-saved-data-06.graded_text: There is no separate tool or argument for setting a site's title, description, or favicon. They come from index.html.

votes.e: C/project/docs/mcp-tools.md line 75: "`title`, `description`, and `faviconPath` are derived from `index.html` on every read, as the brief decides. They aren't stored, and no tool sets them. To change them, edit `index.html`." The create_site schema (lines 199-211) has only workspaceId and address.

blocking: [opus-for-opus2] A large collection can never be overwritten as a whole. Saved data can reach 5 MB per site (line 432), but read_file stops at "about 2,000 lines or 100 KB" (line 283), and line 284 says "Only a `complete: true` read lets a later `write_files` overwrite the file." Inline content is also capped at 256 KB (line 425). Once a collection's file is past about 100 KB, the documented ways to clear test entries and to clear a collection completely (line 139 and line 140, `write_files` the data file) always fail with `conflict`. That leaves only one edit_file call at a time. (held)

[opus-for-opus2] The baseline for overwrite protection is shared too widely. Line 448: "A 'caller' is one OAuth client acting for one user. Two agent sessions on the same connection share what they've read." A second session's stale whole-file write can be merged against a base that a different session read. Entries that a concurrent session changed after this session's read then count as not changed by this caller, so the write can silently revert them. The protection the design promises in line 87 does not hold across parallel sessions. (held)
